exposure: high-volume IV fluids during labor (≥ 2500 mL)
low-volume IV fluids during labor (<2500 mL)
cohort: 1023 women with a live singleton fetus in cephalic presentation, planning a vaginal birth, admitted for labor and birth between 37 and 42 weeks gestation.
finding: High-volume IV fluids during labor (≥2500 mL) was not associated with an increased risk of primary PPH but was positively associated with cesarean section.
mod_finding: High-volume IV fluids during labor (≥2500 mL) was associated with an increased risk of cesarean section compared to low-volume IV fluids (<2500 mL) (ORadj 1.99; 95%CI 1.4, 2.8).
